title: 3D CNN detects pancreatic cancer on diagnostic and some prediagnostic CT scans
summary: A 3D convolutional neural network was trained on 696 diagnostic CTs with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma and 1,080 controls. On the intramural test subset it reached a mean accuracy of 0.92 and an AUROC of 0.97, it was evaluated on multi-institutional public sets (194 cases, 80 controls), and it detected visually occult cancer on prediagnostic CTs. The study is retrospective and case-control; screening utility is simulated.
ai_technology: 3D convolutional neural network on portal-phase CT

evidence.tested: Accuracy on an intramural hold-out set, public multi-institutional data, a simulated screening cohort and a prediagnostic CT cohort.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective case-control design; prospective screening benefit not shown; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: 3D CNN classifying CT scans for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
